questions.stem_tex: The point $(3, -2)$ is reflected across the $y$-axis. Where does it land?
questions.stem_html: The point (3,−2)(3, -2) is reflected across the yy-axis. Where does it land?
questions.solution_tex: Reflecting across the $y$-axis changes the sign of $x$ only: $(x, y) \mapsto (-x, y)$, so $(3, -2) \mapsto (-3, -2)$.

questions.stem_tex: The point $(4, 1)$ is rotated $90^\circ$ counterclockwise about the origin. Where does it land?

questions.stem_tex: A translation maps $A(1, 5)$ to $A'(-2, 7)$. Where does it map $B(4, -3)$?
questions.stem_html: A translation maps A(1,5)A(1, 5) to A′(−2,7)A'(-2, 7). Where does it map B(4,−3)B(4, -3)?
questions.solution_tex: The translation vector is $\langle -2 - 1, 7 - 5 \rangle = \langle -3, 2 \rangle$, so $B(4, -3) \mapsto (4 - 3, -3 + 2) = (1, -1)$.
questions.solution_html: The translation vector is ⟨−2−1,7−5⟩=⟨−3,2⟩\langle -2 - 1, 7 - 5 \rangle = \langle -3, 2 \rangle, so B(4,−3)↦(4−3,−3+2)=(1,−1)B(4, -3) \mapsto (4 - 3, -3 + 2) = (1, -1).

questions.stem_tex: A triangle has vertices $(0, 0)$, $(4, 0)$, $(0, 3)$. It is dilated by a factor of 2 about the origin and then reflected across the $x$-axis. What is the area of the image?
questions.stem_html: A triangle has vertices (0,0)(0, 0), (4,0)(4, 0), (0,3)(0, 3). It is dilated by a factor of 2 about the origin and then reflected across the xx-axis. What is the area of the image?
questions.solution_tex: Reflection does not change area. A dilation by 2 doubles each length, so the legs become 8 and 6 and the area is $\frac{1}{2}(8)(6) = 24$ (four times the original area of 6).
questions.solution_html: Reflection does not change area. A dilation by 2 doubles each length, so the legs become 8 and 6 and the area is 12(8)(6)=24\frac{1}{2}(8)(6) = 24 (four times the original area of 6).

questions.solution_tex: Vertical angles are congruent, so it also measures $35^\circ$.

questions.stem_tex: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle on one side of the transversal measures $(3x + 10)^\circ$ and the other interior angle on the same side measures $(2x + 20)^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.stem_html: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle on one side of the transversal measures (3x+10)∘(3x + 10)^\circ and the other interior angle on the same side measures (2x+20)∘(2x + 20)^\circ. Find xx.
questions.solution_tex: Same-side interior angles are supplementary: $(3x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180$, so $5x + 30 = 180$ and $x = 30$.
questions.solution_html: Same-side interior angles are supplementary: (3x+10)+(2x+20)=180(3x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180, so 5x+30=1805x + 30 = 180 and x=30x = 30.

questions.stem_tex: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of $40^\circ$. What is the measure of each base angle, in degrees?
questions.stem_html: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40∘40^\circ. What is the measure of each base angle, in degrees?
questions.solution_tex: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent and the angles add to $180^\circ$: each base angle is $\frac{180 - 40}{2} = 70^\circ$.
questions.solution_html: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent and the angles add to 180∘180^\circ: each base angle is 180−402=70∘\frac{180 - 40}{2} = 70^\circ.

questions.stem_tex: An exterior angle of a triangle measures $118^\circ$. One of the two remote interior angles measures $47^\circ$. What is the other remote interior angle, in degrees?
questions.stem_html: An exterior angle of a triangle measures 118∘118^\circ. One of the two remote interior angles measures 47∘47^\circ. What is the other remote interior angle, in degrees?
questions.solution_tex: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $118 = 47 + x$, so $x = 71^\circ$.
questions.solution_html: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 118=47+x118 = 47 + x, so x=71∘x = 71^\circ.

questions.stem_tex: Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $DEF$ with $AB = 6$, $DE = 9$ and $BC = 8$. Find $EF$.
questions.stem_html: Triangle ABCABC is similar to triangle DEFDEF with AB=6AB = 6, DE=9DE = 9 and BC=8BC = 8. Find EFEF.
questions.solution_tex: The scale factor from $ABC$ to $DEF$ is $\frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}$, so $EF = 8 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 12$.
questions.solution_html: The scale factor from ABCABC to DEFDEF is 96=32\frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}, so EF=8⋅32=12EF = 8 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 12.

questions.stem_tex: In a right triangle the side opposite angle $\theta$ is 5 and the hypotenuse is 13. What is $\cos\theta$?

questions.solution_tex: The adjacent side is $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{144} = 12$, so $\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{12}{13}$.
questions.solution_html: The adjacent side is 132−52=144=12\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{144} = 12, so cos⁡θ=adjacenthypotenuse=1213\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{12}{13}.

questions.stem_tex: A $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle has a hypotenuse of 10. How long is the side opposite the $60^\circ$ angle?

questions.solution_tex: The sides are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$. The short leg is $10 / 2 = 5$, and the side opposite $60^\circ$ is $5\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem_html: A 6 ft person casts a 4 ft shadow at the same time a tree casts a 30 ft shadow. How tall is the tree, in feet?
questions.solution_tex: The sun makes similar triangles: $\frac{6}{4} = \frac{h}{30}$, so $h = 30 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 45$ ft.
questions.solution_html: The sun makes similar triangles: 64=h30\frac{6}{4} = \frac{h}{30}, so h=30⋅32=45h = 30 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 45 ft.

questions.stem_tex: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1, 2)$, $B(4, 2)$, $C(1, 6)$. Give the vertices of its image after a reflection across the line $y = x$, and explain why the image is congruent to $ABC$.

questions.solution_tex: Reflection across $y = x$ swaps the coordinates: $A'(2, 1)$, $B'(2, 4)$, $C'(6, 1)$. A reflection is a rigid motion (it preserves lengths and angles), so the image is congruent.

questions.stem_tex: A ladder 20 ft long leans against a wall and makes a $70^\circ$ angle with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach? Give the exact form and a decimal to the nearest tenth.
questions.stem_html: A ladder 20 ft long leans against a wall and makes a 70∘70^\circ angle with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach? Give the exact form and a decimal to the nearest tenth.
questions.solution_tex: The wall height is opposite the $70^\circ$ angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse: $h = 20\sin 70^\circ \approx 20(0.9397) \approx 18.8$ ft.
questions.solution_html: The wall height is opposite the 70∘70^\circ angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse: h=20sin⁡70∘≈20(0.9397)≈18.8h = 20\sin 70^\circ \approx 20(0.9397) \approx 18.8 ft.
